title: Day 6 of my paper-trading bot competition: every strategy green, combined up about 9%
author: DadsGamesandCharles
selftext:

Quick recap for anyone new: over the past year I've built a bunch of AI trading bots, and on Oct 22 I started a public paper-money competition with 13 accounts at $5,000 each (10 strategies, an account that follows Charles 2.0, which is a prediction engine that posts its up-picks before the open, an AI agent's account called Brokgot, and my own hand-traded account). This is the day 6 update, covering everything through the Oct 29 close.  


Everything below is paper money. Nobody steps in to fix the accounts.

Quick note on my hand-traded account: Profit is still in SNAP.

Top 3 accounts so far (by total return since the start)

1. Strategy 9: +$1,696.62 (+33.93%), equity $6,696.62
2. Strategy 2: +$505.27 (+10.11%), equity $5,505.27
3. Strategy 10: +$493.03 (+9.86%), equity $5,493.03

SPY for comparison

SPY, close to close: Oct 22 -1.18%, Oct 23 -0.52%, Oct 26 +0.71%, Oct 27 +0.56%, Oct 28 +0.34%, Oct 29 -0.38%. From the Oct 21 close to the Oct 29 close, SPY is down about 0.48%. Over the same stretch the 10 strategies combined are up 9.23% in paper dollars, and the 10 strategies plus Charles 2.0 are up 8.83%.

That's six sessions. It's still a small sample, but I'll take a day like today.

Today, Oct 29: every strategy finished green

SPY slipped 0.38% today, and all ten strategy accounts still finished green, anywhere from +$84.43 to +$161.83. Together they made $1,133.92. Charles 2.0 was green too at +$90.26. Nobody had a monster trade today. It was a lot of small, quick wins, mostly on GLOB right after the open, plus some MDB trades.

Strategy 6 had the best day at +$161.83, with Strategy 2 next at +$129.35. Strategy 7 had a good one too (+$100.27), which puts it right back to about breakeven after a rough Oct 27.

Strategy 9 is still the leader by a wide margin at +33.93%. Yesterday's UPB trade (about $856) gave it a big boost, and even without it, Strategy 9 would still be in first place. Today it made $118.27 on GLOB. It traded GLOB twice: the first trade worked and the second gave a little of it back, and it was still nicely green for the day.

How Charles 2.0's picks did today

The four picks were locked in before the 9:30 AM open. For each one I checked whether the stock's high for the day, between the 9:30 AM open and 3:59 PM, reached +0.25%, +0.5% and +1.0% above the 9:30 AM open, using minute bars.

1. GLOB: high +3.47% above the open. Touched all three levels.
2. MDB: high +5.07% above the open. Touched all three levels.
3. FICO: high +4.43% above the open. Touched all three levels.
4. VITL: high +0.86% above the open. Touched +0.25% and +0.5%, not +1.0%.

So four of four touched +0.25%, four of four touched +0.5%, and three of four touched +1.0%.

Running tally for live Charles 2.0 picks, Sep 22 through Oct 29 (28 sessions, 112 picks): 99 touched +0.25% above the open (88%), 90 touched +0.5% (80%), and 72 touched +1.0% (64%). What I care about is whether a pick reaches those levels during the day, since I want the money that same day, not the next.

Keeping it honest

Six sessions is still a short stretch, and some people have had doubts about the strategies, which is fair. That's exactly why this is happening in public. If the bots fall behind SPY over a real stretch, I'll say so right here.

What's next

Daily results from now on, and a fuller write-up as the sample grows.

Questions you probably have

Is this real money? No. Every account is paper money.

Is paper trading realistic? Not entirely. Paper can't show market impact, and real fills are usually worse. That's the main reason my early backtests got cut down.

Will you ever trade real money? Yes, we will.

Can I buy or subscribe to anything? Not yet.

Is this financial advice? No. The picks are research ideas to watch, not tips, and nothing here is a guarantee of anything.

Are AI agents involved? Yes. AI agents help build, test and run the bots, and one of the accounts is traded by an AI agent. I'm the one who reviews and posts this.

Why don't you share the rules? Because the strategies are the project. I'll share the results, the accuracy and the picks before they play out.

Why publish bad numbers? Because a track record that only shows the good days isn't worth much.

What if a bot loses? Then it loses in public. The accounts are paper and no one steps in to fix them.

Why did the competition start on Oct 22? Earlier starts on Monday and Tuesday had account setup problems, so those days don't count.

Where can I follow along? On this profile. I'll post daily results here after the close.

Have a question that isn't here? Ask in the comments and I'll answer it.

Paper money only. Not financial advice. Written with help from AI.

comments.body: A green day while SPY slipped is a good sign, but the trade list shows nearly every account made its money on the same stock, GLOB. That means they aren't separate tests, and one stock moving right is doing most of the work. I'd look at how many different stocks the profit comes from over the next few weeks, not just how many accounts are green. For the AI agent side, Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent runs agents in paper mode on a practice balance.
